name: Python for Data Science: NumPy, pandas and Notebooks
summary: The scientific stack in your hands: arrays that do not need a loop, DataFrames that survive a real dataset, and a notebook somebody else can actually run.
prerequisites: Requires Python — the language, not the libraries. Statistics helps and is not assumed: the charts here get drawn before they get interpreted.
syllabus: Jupyter, and a notebook that runs from top to bottom
pandas: Series, DataFrame, selection and types
Reproducibility: environments, seeds and data that does not move
topics: Jupyter and JupyterLab: the notebook as a working document
Cells, execution order, and the notebook that only works out of order
Virtual environments, requirements and conda
NumPy: ndarray, dtype and how it sits in memory
Vectorised operations instead of Python loops
Broadcasting: the rule, and the errors it produces
Indexing, slicing and boolean masks
Random numbers, seeds and a result that reproduces
pandas: Series, DataFrame, and the index nobody reads
Reading CSV, Excel, JSON, Parquet and SQL
Selecting with loc and iloc, and the SettingWithCopyWarning
Types, categories, dates and missing values in pandas
groupby: split, apply, combine
merge, join and concat: keys, cardinality and the rows that duplicated
pivot and melt: the wide format and the long one
Rolling, shifting and windows for a series over time
apply and map, and why they are the slow path
matplotlib: figure, axes, and a chart worth publishing
seaborn: distributions, relationships and categories in one line
Memory and speed: dtypes, chunks, and when pandas is the wrong tool
From notebook to script: parameters, functions and a project that runs elsewhere
